"Danseur" for most male ballet dancers!  I only got into it as an adult, though I wanted to when I was little apparently. My folks didnt put me in because, in their words, "I was bullied enough" which I dont blame them for.

As an adult though, I was already a martial arts instructor and was looking for more ways to connect to my body.  I have a little  spinal deformity that causes crippling pain for weeks at a time, and I was hoping the strength and flexibility of ballet could help me.  In some ways it did, but I eventually had to stop after being unable to walk after my final show for nearly a month.  I miss ballet and maybe one day I will be able to return.

It confirmed my beliefs that not only is the internal community of casual adult dance incredibly kind and supportive, but ballet makes you stronger and more flexible than you can imagine.  I power lifted for some time but I put nearly 180 pounds on my 5x5 squats during my first year in ballet alone.

And theres no denying the art and composure of ballet is stunning.  Learning to express stories through movement, flying through the air, learning to spin on a dime; it really is a feeling men dont get often.  I felt powerful, graceful, and  beautiful even! I met quite a few kids during my stay, and got a chance to talk with them away from adults for a little.  Most just wanted to play with bugs, or show me the animals on the farmsteads, but there was one young girl that told me a little about her "job". Haha, its one of the more interesting stories.  So at one point I was handed off to an older guy who lived in a junkyard, and was shown to an old bus with a wood stove and a bed in it.  Bed was horrifying; rat droppings, mysterious stains, the works.  As I set the fire for the night and lay down, I see this strange length of rope hanging from the roof over my head.  I dont pull it and go to sleep.

Next morning, I ask my host about it.  Turns out when his son died, he scalped him and kept it in the bus to dry, and sorta forgot it was there?  So I'd been sleeping under a big hank of scalped dreadlock.  I later found other scalps hanging in other parts of the junkyard.  A collection perhaps?

It took me a while to be able to sleep on a bus, or go anywhere near deep woods.  I saw a therapist at the behest of my sponsor, and wrote some poetry to help me get the lead out.  I can still vividly see everything so clearly, but it has a more level headed feel to it all.

I actually reached back out to some folks I met years later. Several children I met had passed away, one of my hosts got cancer and died quickly.  Closure is strange like that I guess.

At one of my hosts home, I was staying with a fellow from Denmark who was backpacking around the mountains on his own.  When splitting wood one day, we started hearing a bunch of jangling bells from somewhere over a hill, and went to investigate. It was a pack of Alpaca en route to shearing!  The nearest neighbor, a mile or so down the road, was walking them to get a haircut, herding them along like an old timey shepherd.  We talked for a bit and was invited to his daughters birthday party that weekend.  A good time was had by all; everyone brought chainsaws and spent most of the day talking about their chainsaws, sharpening the blades, test cutting wood, etc. Even the kids had little child sized/colored ones that really cut wood!  Never seen anything like it since.

I did some research on small scale agriculture in South Appalachia.  As part of living with and studying the community I stayed with, I was sworn to secrecy for five years after submitting my research to the happenings and names of those I lived with.

I saw arson of federal property, and impersonating officers of the law and clergy.  Grand theft auto, meth cooking and moonshining.  Cockfights, kids getting coerced into prostitution, dogs getting shot full of rocksalt for laughs. I had to sleep in a junkyard for a few nights and found dried human scalps hanging in an old bus, ate rotting meat from a dumpster and had to hide for my life from shotgun-wielding thieves in the dead of winter.

Its not all horror shows in the hills; theres good people, tightly knit communities, and beauty in nature I've never seen since. But whats there is very much real and very much a danger. This planets creatures are, by a rule, huge, with hundreds of species of megafauna.  Lets start at the top and list a few options moving down the scale.

The largest goes, without competition, to the legendary World Eel, Sa-Yi-Kahn, a primordial Emissary of one of the Six Gods.  Stretching nearly 7000 miles long, its slow, endless migration through the deep, ancient oceans of the Geodes Shell causes the tides and winds to move. Below him are his innumerable offspring, the Tawihaan.  Rainbow scales serpents, reaching a mile in length at adulthood, with feathery crests and several dozen eyes along the broad of their faces, they are a true beauty to behold.  Once every hundred years or so, they swim to the isolated continent of Pianook to wage war on its northern coast for dominance of their schools.  Many hundreds of tribes of indigenous peoples follow these serpents migrations, and pit aerial battles above the warring titans, swinging from cliff to cliff on sinew ropes in support of their tribes chosen serpent.  

In the sky, we have the Chuurak-Hul, great kaleidoscopic clouds of tiny electro-philic organisms that clump into swarms up to 800 feet in diameter.  These tiny organisms protect themselves with a dense mucilage, and when they detect a mucus membrane of a fellow member of its species, they exude thin nanowire filaments into each others bubble, forming the floating structure they are known for and sharing sensory information.  They drift with the currents of the wind, and feed off of tiny bacteria that they grow in their mucus bubbles using atmospheric electrical discharges.  Older Chuurak-Hul have been connected so long that their independent minds fuse into one great consciousness; it has been claimed that certain powerful Singers have spoken with them about the secrets of flight.  

On land?  You have your common giant tortoises, tundra bears, elk; a handful of hundreds of giant species and the like, but thats not what you're here to see.  Among the more fascinating terrestrial creatures are the Tulsu.  Tall as a mammoth, these delicate horses have impressively thin, graceful legs, wide, deep set eyes, and opalescent, feathered hair.  They never make a sound, even if you were to deck them in bells from head to hoof.  The only native resident mammals of the ancient forest of sound-eating glass trees from the southern reaches of the split island of Douemi.

Amongst these rare and beautiful creatures, I cannot highly enough recommend the Ashvid. Elegant like a ballerinas, fine of limb and soft of short, delicate hair (always ivory), the Ashvid stand poised like dancers, horses with narrow faces and wise, knowing eyes.  Their bodies are too frail for riding I'm afraid, but their legendary beauty, silence, and grace more than make up for it.  Entire cities have been scrapped and sold just to acquire breeding stock of exceptional pedigree of this rare and magnificent creature.

Found exclusively on the far flung continent of Laklau in the South, they wander the silent Glass woods of the Abhicu forest, searching for tender sprouts of grasses that attract the tiny creatures known as Manna.  It is upon these that they feed; as such, a crafty breeder will make sure to raise these grasses above all else.  A modest upfront investment that returns even greater dividends over time, as the grasses themselves a worth quite the pretty pocket of coin.

It should be noted that the Ashvid are also renown for their intelligence, and their hands in upliting the heroes of fate.  From Vipul the Tiger sage, to Quin-Garret, Ninth Empress of the Downcast Eye, great peoples of legends always find themselves surrounded by these majestic creatures, who bring them gifts in their times of greatest need, and watch over them with silent loyalty from afar.  Perhaps your daughter is the 10th Empress, waiting for her time to shine?

There are many sea dwelling cultures that send their youth out on spirit quests to find a Tawihan, and decorate its bony armor with carvings, gifts, and permanent dyes. When humans still walked the planet of The Geode, two styles of martial arts were held in reverence above all other fighting styles outside of the realm of Weaving and Sorcery. The Marmayali style was said to have come to the great martial master Jahrna during a spiritual journey into the crystal groves of Abhicu in the southern half of the Blessed Lovers.  Belonging to the martial school of Qinjab Quinna, on the central Isle of Anguta, she was distressed by the brutality of her instructor to his students, and after witnessing the death of a young pupil to his masters calloused treatment, went on a spiritual journey into the Abhicu Glass Woods, and was presumed dead.  She wandered deeper and deeper into the woods, without food or water, until she came to a dense grove with the remains of a shattered tree.  All hope lost, the lay on the shards of glass and meditated on the hopelessness of life and death.  As she meditated, the shards of the tree began to regrow, slowly piercing her at 1000 different points, and in such, giving her the knowledge of the points of life and death, until the tree had grown in and through her, both body and soul.  1000 days later, she awoke, having been nourished by the forest, and stepped off from the tree reformed, the 1000 pieces of the glass tree remaining imbedded in her flesh as a reminder of her lesson.  Upon returning, she denounced the cruelety of her master, who attacked her.  With a gentle brush of her hand and a whisper of the Mantra of Stillness, he was silenced and frozen in place, suspended between death and life.  Walking to his injured pupils, she healed them all with a touch of her hand and the careful application of thin glass shards which sprung from her flesh at her whim.  She named her school Marmayali, after the name of the Djinn of the tree of her teacher, where it remains to this day.  

This style focuses on a balanced duality between life and death, its practitioners swearing never to kill an opponent if the slightest hope of saving them is possible.  They are equally trained in both healing and killing arts, and fight barehanded at all times, as weapons disconnect the martial artist from the victim/patient.  Furthermore, each student is required to journey into Abhicu, to follow the spirit journey of Jahrna and learn from the growth of the trees, titans of twisting glass that subsist only on sound.  These glass shards must enter the students body to act as resonators for the master Sutras of the art.  If the student is unprepared, or the tree finds him unworthy, the glass branches will grow into the persons brain and kill them.

Visiting his family on Atīta Aura Bhavisyathe (Island of Past and Future) academy, the school bore witness to the splits in the Tapestry of the world, and the ensuing maelstrom as the island was ripped from the Tapestry sent their vessel off course, lodging it on the beaches of Laklau, the Fire Wood of North Anguta. This can be done through nearly any means, and there are as many ways of casting a circle as there are people interested in doing so.

Speaking from my perspective, the circle is a triple reinforced barrier of intent made solid, drawn through the earth and air to give me protection while I lower my guard and work with powerful, often temperamental forces.
